$comment: GOLDEN CONTRACT FIXTURE — engine-command envelope v1 (issue #4539).
An `@agent-engine` command reaches the orchestration engine as a DynamoDB row,
not as a call. The webhook-ingress Lambda writes the row after verifying
GitHub's HMAC; the gateway-side orchestration tick reads it back and treats its
fields as WHO acted, in WHICH tenant, on WHICH plan. This contract is the
cryptographic binding between those two halves: the signer commits to the exact
authority-and-routing tuple, and the verifier refuses anything it cannot
reproduce.
The two implementations live in SEPARATE DEPLOY UNITS and cannot import each
other — the Lambda is a zip, the tick runs in the gateway container image. That
is the same constraint that already forces ENGINE_COMMAND_STATUS_* to be
re-declared on both sides. Canonicalization is therefore written twice, and this
file is what pins the pair:
signer   modules/agent-factory/webhook-ingress/lambda/common/command_signing.py
verifier modules/gateway/src/orchestration/command_attribution.py
Both test suites read these vectors and assert byte-for-byte canonical output and
signature equality. A canonicalization change on one side without the other
breaks those tests here, rather than silently refusing every real human command
in production — which is the failure mode this fixture exists to prevent.
The signing key below is a PUBLISHED TEST VALUE and must never appear in any
deployed environment. Real keys live only in Secrets Manager, are never in
Terraform state, git or logs, and are readable by exactly the signer and verifier
roles — no worker, source or supervisor identity.
Each vector's `why` states the confusion it catches. They are not decorative:
every one is a place where two independent implementations of 'canonical JSON'
plausibly diverge while both looking correct in review.
canonical_form: UTF-8 JSON array of [name, value] pairs in `field_order`, separators (',',':'), ensure_ascii=False. An ARRAY rather than an object because JSON objects carry no inherent order: 'both sides sort the keys' is a convention that holds until someone adds a field, whereas a positional array makes the order part of the data.

vectors.name: ascii_halt
vectors.why: Plain single-line ASCII command — the ordinary case.

vectors.name: unicode_body
vectors.why: Non-ASCII body. Canonical bytes are UTF-8, never \uXXXX escapes: a signer using ensure_ascii=True and a verifier using False would disagree on every non-English command.

envelope.command_body: @agent-engine replan: rollback der Änderung — 日本語 🚀

vectors.canonical_utf8: [["protocol_version","1"],["key_id","2026-09"],["provider","github"],["delivery_id","d1e2f3a4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"],["event_type","issue_comment"],["event_id","msg-0001"],["arrived_at","2026-09-15T21:15:31Z"],["tenant_id","acme-corp"],["installation_id","99887766"],["repo_id",123456789],["repo","acme-corp/flagship-app"],["issue_number",4539],["sender_github_id","1042"],["sender_type","User"],["command_body","@agent-engine replan: rollback der Änderung — 日本語 🚀"],["signed_at","2026-09-15T21:15:32Z"]]

vectors.name: embedded_newlines
vectors.why: Multi-line body with CR, LF and tab. JSON string escaping is what makes these survive; a line-joined signing input would collapse them.

vectors.name: numeric_types_are_not_strings
vectors.why: repo_id and issue_number are JSON numbers. The string spellings sign to a DIFFERENT value, so neither side may coerce between them.

vectors.name: bot_sender
vectors.why: GitHub's author kind is a SIGNED field, so 'a bot did not ask for anything' rests on verified ingress rather than on a mutable row flag.

vectors.name: json_metacharacters_in_body
vectors.why: Quotes, backslashes and brackets in the body. Proves body content cannot restructure the canonical array and forge a neighbouring field.

vectors.name: empty_command_body
vectors.why: An empty body still signs. Emptiness is not absence: an unsigned row and a row signed over an empty body must stay distinguishable.

rejected_variants.name: object_with_sorted_keys
rejected_variants.why_rejected: Reads as canonical and is not. Key order becomes an emergent property of the field NAMES, so renaming a field silently reorders the signed bytes, and each side's idea of 'sorted' has to agree about non-ASCII names. A positional array makes order explicit data that a vector can pin.

rejected_variants.name: colon_joined_string
rejected_variants.why_rejected: Field-injection. A body containing ':' can shift the boundaries so one signed string parses as a different tuple — the classic length-extension-adjacent confusion. JSON string escaping removes the class entirely.

rejected_variants.name: ensure_ascii_true
rejected_variants.why_rejected: Works for every English command and fails for the first accented or CJK replan text, in production, as a total refusal of that user's commands. The unicode_body vector is what catches it in CI instead.

rejected_variants.name: signature_over_the_row
rejected_variants.shape: sign(the DynamoDB item as read back)
rejected_variants.why_rejected: The row carries unsigned attributes too (status, TTL, correlation fields), and some are legitimately mutated after the write — the consume flip is one. A signature over the whole row would either break on every legitimate update or have to enumerate exclusions, which is the field spec again with worse failure modes.

rejected_variants.name: reuse_the_marker_signing_key
rejected_variants.why_rejected: The agent worker role is granted a purpose-scoped kms:Decrypt for the marker-signing key so it can sign correlation markers (webhook-ingress/infra/scaledjob-iam.tf, issue #4028). Reusing it here would hand the ability to MINT human approval attribution to the exact identity the authority boundary exists to constrain.

rejected_variants.name: verify_after_identity_lookup
rejected_variants.shape: resolve the commenter, then check the signature
rejected_variants.why_rejected: Not a canonicalization choice but the ordering it implies, so it is recorded here: every field is attacker-chosen until the signature verifies. Resolving an identity, an installation or a plan from an unverified row uses forged input for a side effect and leaks existence through timing and through the reply's destination.
